channel.description: Latest articles from Al-Jazeera Media Network (aljazeera.com)

item.title: More than 200 killed in mine collapse in eastern DR Congo: Report
item.description: Rights groups have raised concerns over conditions at the mine, which supplies about 15 percent of the world's coltan.

item.title: T20 World Cup 2026 stadiums: Where’s India vs Pakistan and the final?
item.description: Al Jazeera’s guide to the eight venues that will host the T20 World Cup 2026 matches in India and Sri Lanka.

item.title: Brief US government shutdown begins after funding deadline lapses
item.description: US gov't funding impasse driven by Democratic anger over federal agents killing two people during immigration crackdown.

item.title: US approves $6.6bn sale of attack helicopters, assault vehicles to Israel
item.description: The approved sale includes 30 Apache helicopters, which Israeli forces have used to attack Palestinians in Gaza.

item.title: Myanmar election delivers walkover win for military-backed political party
item.description: Myanmar's military rulers say polls were free and fair as UN reports 170 killed during election period.

item.title: How does ICE spend its budget? And who profits?
item.description: ICE now has a larger budget than the FBI, bigger even than the militaries of 170 countries. So where does that money go?

item.title: LIVE: Iran announces live-fire naval drills near US warships amid tensions
item.description: US army warns Iran that it will not tolerate 'unsafe' manoeuvres such as flights over US warships.

item.title: Venezuela’s acting President Delcy Rodriguez announces prisoner amnesty
item.description: Rodriguez calls for healing 'wounds left by political confrontation' and says notorious El Helicoide prison to shut.

item.title: Wave of Israeli air strikes hit southern Lebanon despite ceasefire
item.description: Israeli air strikes pound areas in southern Lebanon in violation of the November 2024 ceasefire with Hezbollah.

item.title: Shipping giant Maersk to take over Panama Canal ports after court ruling
item.description: Danish company will replace Hong Kong-based firm after Trump claimed strategic waterway was controlled by China.
